en: Homage to the glorious Ekallavīra, the benefactor of all sentient beings, whose body is the single embodiment of the three bodies (kāyas) that utterly destroys obstacles. || 1 ||
With his right hand he holds a drawn sword by way of means (*upāya*),
and with his left hand, which embodies wisdom (*prajñā*), he holds a noose attached to the forefinger.
Salutations to the one who looks downward with his left eye for the sake of protecting the seven netherworlds,
and salutations to the one who looks upward with his right [eye] due to his role as the protector of the seven cosmic eggs.
Homage to you, who have placed your left knee upon the ground for the sake of protecting it, and whose right foot is positioned for the abandonment of Māra.
Homage to you, Lord Akṣobhya, who wears a crest-jewel of his own [seed-]syllable,
who is adorned with variegated garments and ornaments, and who possesses the vajra of the two equal states.
Salutations to the one who destroyed Brahmā, Indra, and the Daitya Śūlapāṇi;
salutations to the illustrious Caṇḍaroṣa, whose rays exceed a hundred thousand suns.
Emptiness is expressed by the syllable *a*, great bliss by the syllable *ca*, and the unity of these two by the syllable *la*; therefore, homage be to you, O Acala! (7)
Fulfilled by twice eight perfections, arising from moments that are distinct, and because you are unshakable even through dispassion—for that reason as well, homage be to you! (8)
Dispassion is conceived as Caṇḍa because of the slaying [of passion]; from that arises wrath and the dawning of the King of Bliss. Therefore, homage to you, Caṇḍaroṣaṇa! 9.
Salutation with my head to you, whose nature is perfected bliss, at whose rising the sense objects, along with the senses themselves, go to their setting. 10.
Homage to you, whose nature is the syllable of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) endowed with the excellence of all aspects, appearing like a reflection in a mirror. 11.
Having praised you, who are beyond praise and difficult to perceive even for the stainless ones, whatever merit has been acquired by me, may all beings become steadfast through it. 12.
Thus ends the hymn to the two stages of Acala.
This is the work of the venerable master Vanaratna.
